full_judgment:
3. The petitioners and opposite Party No. 3 as defendants contested the said suit by filing separate written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint. Their case was that the opposite party No. 3 was owner of 3.99 acres of land out of which he sold 0.80 acres to one Kanchon Ali Khan and thereafter he gifted 1.80 acres of land out of the remaining land to the petitioners by a registered deed of gift dated 17.4.75 and delivered possession thereof to them. The petitioners were possessing the same since then. Their further case was that the mortgage land were redeemed before the execution of the aforesaid deed of gift. The petitioners also averred that opposite party No. 3 agreed to mortgage 0.20 acres and 0.10 acres of land for Tk. 600 and 300/- respectively out of the remaining land after the transfer made by the deed of gift to the plaintiffs opposite party Nos. 1 and 2. But they fraudulently and collusively obtained the disputed kabalas without consideration instead of taking mortgage by patta. They also alleged that the kabalas were not acted upon and the plaintiff opposite parties had no right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit. 

 It appears that the said court arrived at the aforesaid finding without at all considering the question of prior talk as to sale before the kabalas and referring the evidences on record in this respect. The finding of the lower appellate court that opposite party No. 3 got the consideration money by adjusting the pattani amount is also based on no evidence. 

 7. As to the finding of redemption by the lower appellate court is concerned it was based on no evidence as well. The same was based on the reasoning’s that a prudent man would not take a new patta for a land of which he was already in possession on the basis of an earlier patta without taking into consideration any evidence on record and as such the same was based merely on assumption.
